claude.sample_unit: adult patient long-term EEG monitoring recordings

links.outcome: Diagnostic sensitivity of expert-supervised AI (hybrid) versus conventional review
links.effect: Hybrid sensitivity .88 (95% CI .77-.97) vs conventional .69 (.57-.81), adjusted p = .006; interrater AC1 .81 vs .43; review time reduced 95.8%.
links.quote: The hybrid approach showed significantly higher sensitivity than conventional interpretation (.88, 95% CI = .77-.97 vs. .69, 95% CI = .57-.81; adjusted p = .006).

links.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of expert-reviewed AI versus fully automated AI analysis
links.effect: Hybrid accuracy .75 (95% CI .66-.83) vs fully automated .55 (.44-.65); adjusted p < .001.
links.quote: Hybrid approach diagnostic accuracy was significantly greater than fully automated analysis (.75, 95% CI = .66-.83 vs. .55, 95% CI = .44-.65; adjusted p < .001).

links.outcome: Accuracy of AI as adjunct with expert oversight versus stand-alone automated use
links.effect: Expert-supervised hybrid accuracy .75 vs fully automated .55 (adjusted p < .001); hybrid sensitivity higher than conventional.
links.quote: Expert oversight of AI-assisted categorization of interictal epileptiform and nonepileptiform EEG abnormalities improves interrater reliability and efficiency, increases diagnostic sensitivity versus conventional interpretation, and increases diagnostic accuracy versus fully automated analysis in adult LTM.
